statement: The call coordination contract accepts a versioned canonical structured partial value with a closed type grammar and explicit byte/count budgets; guests and hosts agree on one encoding, malformed or oversized values fail closed, replay is byte-stable, reducer input is deterministic, and duplicate cross-shard key semantics are explicit rather than silently merged. Verified at HEAD 761dc17c7: partials must parse to finite numbers, enforced at two fail-closed gates (call-cell-routing-contract.js normalizeEmittedPartialEntries and call-cell-reduce-coordinator.js), with cross-shard group keys required disjoint (SHARD_OVERLAP refusal).

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn an independent verifier before audit and handoff and record its stable evidence id.
The routing contract and reduce coordinator remain the owners of partial validation and merge; one canonical encoding owner exists. No second partial codec.

First scope: null, boolean, safe integer, finite float, string, bounded list, bounded record with lexical field order; no arbitrary object prototype or executable data; one canonical binary or canonical JSON encoding owner; retain disjoint keys for the first release unless an algebraic merge contract is separately specified; expose generated editor types from the code-first compiler.

Existing numeric partials remain compatible: the account summary example moves to one structured record per shard while previously valid numeric-key partials continue to validate and reduce unchanged.
Malformed, oversized, prototype-polluting, or non-canonical values must fail closed; silently merging duplicate cross-shard keys (double-counting) must fail deterministically.
